target_customer: Parents, family and friends who want to save for a child through a simple online trust
problem: Setting up a trust for a child is expensive and complicated; TrustEgg let parents create one free and let others contribute, invested in Vanguard funds.
business_model: Asset-based fee of 89 basis points a year on assets under management, covering the Vanguard fund fee

founders.name: Jeffrey Brice
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch 2013 says he had been focused on the idea for years; no employers or schools found in opened sources.

founders.name: Gabe Krambs
founders.background_notes: YC bio lists later ventures Compound and CS DISCO (IPO 2021). TechCrunch 2013 says he left TrustEgg to take a job that paid the bills.

founders.name: John Zdanowski
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder, CFO and investor in TechCrunch 2013; not on the YC page and not day to day.

exit.reason: Not public; YC lists the company as inactive.

technical_complexity.rationale: A consumer front end on top of a licensed trust company and Vanguard funds; the hard parts were compliance and operations, not software.

defensibility.rationale: The product ran as a licensed product of Summit Trust rather than its own chartered trust company, so the regulatory position was borrowed and replicable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source describes an incumbent copying or buying the product.

market_need_then: TechCrunch 2013 describes a program for lower income families (1:1 Fund) working with TrustEgg, and the founder's multi-year focus on democratizing trusts, but no spend or demand figures were found.

branding.domain_note: YC lists fidoosh.com (the holding company Fidoosh, Inc.); the product used trustegg.com in 2013 coverage.

identity.logo: An image appears in TechCrunch but no text describes it
identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline: the simple, social way to save for a child's future

brand_strength.rationale: Demoed at FinovateSpring 2013 and covered by TechCrunch, but no brand-driven growth documented.

outcome_analysis: TrustEgg was a YC W11 company that hit a regulatory standstill in August 2012, moved to San Diego and launched in February 2013 as a licensed product of Summit Trust, with $100K from Foresight Ventures; one co-founder had already left. A database lists a $1M seed in December 2013. YC lists it as inactive, but no shutdown notice or post-mortem was found, so the cause is not public and no failure factors are asserted.
notes: The 2013-12 $1M seed rests on a single database (StartupIntros, listing angels Howard Love and Paul Stahura plus a long investor list I did not trust and did not record). Seedtable totals $1.15M over two rounds; CB Insights shows $20K over three rounds and still tags the company Alive; sources conflict. Total of recorded rounds is $1.1M. The competitors list is empty: TechCrunch names none and one dated search found no rivals near 2011; ugift and 529 plans appeared only in undated or later pages. The fidoosh.com site returned HTTP 503. A trademark record shows TRUSTEGG as abandoned in 2011 (aggregator snippet).
